# BurnZombies agent setup and operation

Canonical guide: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swordfish444/BurnZombies/main/llms.txt
Repository: https://github.com/swordfish444/BurnZombies
Supported harnesses: Codex and Claude Code. Requires macOS 14+, Apple Silicon or Intel, and an installed, signed-in harness.

## Installation is not cleanup

Install/configure only what the operator requested. Never run a hunt, approve a burn, grant automatic cleanup, stop a process or retire a worktree as an installation test. Do not change credentials, account routing, global MCP configuration, chat hooks or shell profiles. Preserve existing model/provider selections. Account/permission refusal means pause, never provider fallback.

## Fresh installation

Check `sw_vers -productVersion` and either `codex --version` or `claude --version`. CLI availability alone does not prove authentication. Download and inspect the installer, then execute it with the chosen harness:

```sh
installer="$(mktemp -t burnzombies-installer)"
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swordfish444/BurnZombies/main/install.sh -o "$installer"
bash "$installer" --mcp codex --observe-only
rm "$installer"
```

For Claude Code, use `--mcp claude --observe-only` in the same command. The observer starts in the background. `--observe-only` configures the private integration but leaves AI reviews disabled; native inventory can still run. The installer checks the release checksum, archive paths and bundle signature. Current releases are ad-hoc signed, not notarized. If macOS blocks opening, report the actual prompt; do not disable Gatekeeper or remove quarantine metadata.

Verify using the bundled CLI (no global command or PATH edit is needed):

```sh
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" version
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" doctor
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" access-status
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" findings
```

Substitute the operator's explicit BURNZOMBIES_INSTALL_DIR if used. Check doctor.configuredHarness, configuredExecutableAvailable, mcpServerAvailable, appResponding and runningAppMatchesCLI. `version`/`build` identify this CLI; `runningAppVersion`/`runningAppBuild` identify the responding app. An old or mismatched app is not a verified update. Unknown permission/coverage or an empty inbox is not a successful discovery test.

Full Disk Access is optional: without it BurnZombies covers everything except the places macOS protects (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive, Mail, Messages, Photos, other apps' data, external drives) and AI hunts stay off. Granting it requires the human: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access → add/enable the exact installed BurnZombies.app. `access-check` verifies an existing grant; it cannot grant access. Recovery may require the human to answer a Keychain prompt. Never bypass these permission boundaries. Report pending human steps honestly.

Show the operator the menu bar's Autopilot line, Teach BZ (yes/no questions that teach rules) and Findings. Autopilot sweeps every 15 minutes: it burns orphaned programs, retires old copies (always restorable) and clears rebuildable junk folders that its starter rules or the operator's answers cover, and asks about the rest. Settings → Autopilot turns it off or changes the frequency. See docs/AUTOPILOT.md. Review permission is not blanket cleanup permission. Finding notifications are controlled in Findings → Notifications and workflow rules → Notify me about findings. Notification permission and details visibility are separate choices; do not enable them silently as an install test.

## Existing installation / update

Read version, doctor and access-status first. Preserve the selected harness, model, thinking effort, schedule and enabled/paused state. Run the inspected installer with `--mcp auto`; omit --observe-only unless the operator asked to disable reviews. No fallback occurs if the selected harness is missing. The installer gracefully closes only its exact previous app bundle; it refuses a forced replacement if shutdown fails.

For an explicitly requested provider selection:

```sh
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" setup --harness codex
# OR, only when the operator selected Claude Code:
"$HOME/Applications/BurnZombies.app/Contents/MacOS/burnzombies" setup --harness claude
```

Optional explicit selections: --model MODEL_ID, --thinking high (or another supported level), --model default, --thinking default. Setup writes BurnZombies's private configuration and preserves unspecified prior settings. Run doctor afterward. It never grants new cleanup authority. Existing native policies retain their original guards.

## Codex

The resident app launches an owned, bounded Codex app-server session for each focused review and supplies its private MCP server. No always-loaded global MCP server, working-chat skill, hooks or global config edit is required. Do not run the legacy install/install-skill commands for normal setup. Existing chat permissions and global Codex settings remain the user's.

## Claude Code

The resident app uses the installed Claude Code CLI and existing login, with focused instructions, a private MCP configuration and a bounded turn allowance. Unrelated MCP servers, project hooks and browser integration are excluded from this background invocation. No edit to ~/.claude.json or ~/.claude/settings.json is required. Ordinary chats are unaffected.

## Read-only diagnosis

- doctor: configuration and app connectivity; no cleanup or model invocation.
- access-status: permission state; access-check: recheck an existing grant.
- findings [OFFSET]: durable inbox; blocked/unknown is not zero.
- Native Worktrees window: discovered checkouts, evidence gaps and recovery history.
- Private reviewer MCP tool burnzombies_worktrees with action list or operations: inventory or native receipts. These are MCP calls, not CLI subcommands; normal setup does not add them to unrelated chats.
- evidence PID [PID ...]: up to 16 exact current process identities; no signals.
- status: saved aggregate catalog; does not prove the running app responds.

Hunt now starts an Autopilot sweep immediately; it is not an installation test. `burnzombies autopilot` prints the current snapshot (counts, open questions, learned rules) without changing anything. Native inventory continues without a model. Age, size, a finished chat turn or a merged PR alone never proves abandonment. Missing owner/consumer evidence preserves the resource.

New idle worktrees appear for manual review without prompting. Worktree notifications require the configured stale age (fourteen days by default), an exact completion confirmation, or released current owners. These signals request attention; they do not grant cleanup authority.

## Decisions and recovery

Findings shows the exact action, evidence, protection and recovery requirement. Keep protects that identity across action paths. Approval once applies to one semantic revision and is revalidated before dispatch. Recurring rules are separate grants with exact scope, cap, expiry and a one-item canary; success never expands them. Silence, dismissal and snooze never approve cleanup.

Gradle adapters support exactly 8.14.6 and 9.8.2 via authenticated StopWhenIdle: raced builds finish before exit. Generic process stops require positive ownership and completion evidence. Worktree retirement requires management/release, complete inspection and independently verified encrypted recovery. Harness-owned worktrees stay with their owning tool. Only verified native receipts count as cleanup; uncertain dispatches are never automatically retried.

Report installation, permission readiness, actual model review, surfaced findings and verified cleanup separately. Destructive acceptance tests must use sacrificial targets, never real work.
